title: The “Warrior Ethos” Promises Victory, History Says It Leads to Defeat
author: John Broich
content:
[![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/05/Pete_Hegseth_51328588107-680x453.jpg)](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/05/26/the-
warrior-ethos-promises-victory-history-says-it-leads-to-defeat/)

![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/05/Pete_Hegseth_51328588107-680x453.jpg)

Photograph Source: Gage Skidmore - [CC BY-Sa
2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/)

At Marine Corps Base Quantico in September 2025, [Defense Secretary Pete
Hegseth promised assembled generals](https://www.airandspaceforces.com/read-
hegseth-speech-generals-admirals/) “maximum lethality” and no “stupid rules of
engagement.” Under his leadership, the [newly rebranded Department of
War](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/trump-administration/trump-executive-
order-rebrands-defense-department-war-department-rcna229461) would “untie the
hands of our warfighters to intimidate, demoralize, hunt, and kill.” Troops
would be held to the “[highest male
standard](https://www.airandspaceforces.com/read-hegseth-speech-generals-
admirals/),” he said. “Weak men won’t qualify.”

Hegseth also [restricted anonymous whistleblower and discrimination
complaints](https://www.adn.com/nation-world/2025/09/30/hegseth-to-upend-
troops-access-to-watchdog-ability-to-file-whistleblower-complaints/) and
[limited how long past misconduct can be held against a service
member](https://abcnews.com/Politics/hegseths-policy-memos-hazing-harassment-
military/story?id=126081286), weakening internal rules and oversight processes
the military had built over decades.

Months later, with the Iran war underway, [he told reporters at a Pentagon
briefing](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/pete-hegseth-declares-iran-
not-133442887.html) that the U.S. was “punching (Iran) while they’re down,
which is exactly how it should be.” [He has also
said](https://www.war.gov/News/Transcripts/Transcript/Article/4434484/secretary-
of-war-pete-hegseth-and-chairman-of-the-joint-chiefs-air-force-gen-da/) the
U.S. will give “no quarter, no mercy” to its enemies, language legal experts
say can constitute [a war crime under international
law](https://www.justsecurity.org/133970/legal-advice-hegseth-no-quarter-
hypo/).

[Hegseth calls his military doctrine](https://www.airandspaceforces.com/read-
hegseth-speech-generals-admirals/) the “warrior ethos.”

[Historians of fascism](https://theconversation.com/what-is-fascism-153947)
have [catalogued similar rhetorical
patterns](https://www.nybooks.com/articles/1995/06/22/ur-fascism/) — strongman
posturing, contempt for constraint — for decades.

I’m [a historian of race and
nationalism](https://history.case.edu/faculty/john-broich/) and author of
“[Blood, Oil and the Axis](https://www.abramsbooks.com/product/blood-oil-and-
the-axis_9781468314014/),” a book about World War II and nationalism in Iraq
and Syria. I’ve studied how fascist regimes fight. At its core, [fascism is
ultranationalism](https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/128540/the-anatomy-
of-fascism-by-robert-o-paxton/) fused with a cult of masculine strength,
racial hierarchy, paranoia about socialism and contempt for democracy. It also
has a theory of war: Victory belongs to the ruthless and the ideologically
pure. Rules are for the weak.

Nazi Germany, fascist Italy and Imperial Japan all built their military
strategies on some version of this ideology in the run-up to the Second World
War. And in each case, the strategy failed, undone by its own contradictions.

**The Fascist Theory of War**

Democracies don’t necessarily fight clean wars. During World War II, the
Allies [firebombed
cities](https://www.nationalww2museum.org/war/articles/apocalypse-dresden-
february-1945), [created internment
camps](https://www.britannica.com/event/Japanese-American-internment) and
[dropped atomic bombs](https://www.britannica.com/event/atomic-bombings-of-
Hiroshima-and-Nagasaki).

What distinguishes fascist powers from democracies is their contempt for rules
based on their sense of superiority. In 1933, [Adolf Hitler’s propaganda
minister Joseph Goebbels announced](https://research.calvin.edu/german-
propaganda-archive/goeb23.htm) that the Nazis would claim the absolute right
to override democratic constraints. “This contemptible parliamentarianism … is
gone,” he said.

Italian dictator Benito Mussolini [said it more
bluntly](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Benito_Mussolini) in 1936: “We do not
argue with those who disagree with us, we destroy them.”

But [rules of engagement function as a control
system](https://www.military.com/feature/2026/03/05/hegseths-stupid-rules-of-
engagement-line-and-what-roe-actually-do.html) that ties tactical decisions to
strategy, law and the risk of escalation. Discarding them tends to produce the
atrocities and strategic blowback that lose wars.

Democratic procedure does similar work: Political scientists who studied 197
[conflicts from 1816 to 1987](https://millercenter.org/democracies-have-edge-
fighting-wars) found that democracies won about 76% of their conflicts and
non-democracies 46%, in large part because accountable leaders and public
access to information force a government to notice when a plan isn’t working.

A fascist regime that treats democratic constraints as obstacles is likely to
decide inconvenient information is an obstacle too. Because of this, in
fascist governments, loyalists rank higher than experts. Fascist systems don’t
remove people for being wrong; they remove them for [insufficient
loyalty](https://www.newsweek.com/were-hitlers-generals-loyal-historians-
verdicts-1976569). The man who tells the leader what he wants to hear rises.
The man whose report contradicts the leader’s views endangers himself.

## The Closed Circuit

Consider [Joachim von
Ribbentrop](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Joachim-von-Ribbentrop).

Before becoming Hitler’s foreign minister, he was a wine salesman whose [years
in Canada](https://www.historicalsocietyottawa.ca/publications/ottawa-
stories/personalities-from-the-very-famous-to-the-lesser-known/rib) became his
qualification for understanding America. He attached himself to Hitler and was
rewarded with a top seat in his government, where [Ribbentrop’s signature
contribution](https://doi.org/10.1017/9781108870405.003) was overruling the
diplomats who warned that Americans would fight if pushed too far by the Axis.

The Nazi view prevailed: Americans were too racially mixed, too soft, too
consumed by money to be dangerous. When Germany declared war on the U.S. four
days after Pearl Harbor, it did so partly on that disdain for what Hitler
called a “[mongrel nation](https://historynet.com/hitlers-dark-
december-1941/).” Ribbentrop was among the most consequentially wrong foreign
ministers in modern history – he’d also misjudged [Britain’s willingness to
join the war](https://www.history.com/articles/world-war-ii-begins-german-
invasion-poland-1939) over the invasion of Poland – still, he kept his job.

The ideology that produced Ribbentrop’s overconfidence also produced the Nazi
theory of the Eastern Front: that Slavic peoples – [fundamentally inferior and
tainted by
Bolshevism](https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/article/victims-of-the-
nazi-era-nazi-racial-ideology) – would collapse within weeks. But [the Red
Army didn’t collapse](https://www.iwm.org.uk/history/second-world-
war/operation-barbarossa-and-germanys-failure-in-the-soviet-union). Hitler
[fired the
officers](https://www.usni.org/magazines/proceedings/1956/may/hitler-and-
german-officer-corps) who reported as much and demanded more of the same
operations that had already failed. [Operation
Barbarossa](https://www.britannica.com/event/Operation-Barbarossa), which was
supposed to take weeks, stretched to years.

Attempting to match Hitler’s conquests and assert dominance over the
Mediterranean, Mussolini invaded Greece in October 1940 with shorthanded
divisions, in mountain terrain and at the start of winter, because he believed
Italian spirit would overwhelm Greek resistance in two weeks. [His generals
had doubts](https://historynet.com/neither-loved-nor-hated-field-marshal-
pietro-badoglio/), but many [did not express them](https://www.lrb.co.uk/the-
paper/v42/n10/edward-luttwak/not-uniquely-incompetent). The Greeks
counterattacked, but Mussolini blamed his generals’ “[insufficient
will](https://api.pageplace.de/preview/DT0400.9780313072499_A47347892/preview-9780313072499_A47347892.pdf),”
the only kind of failure his theory allowed. Germany had to intervene.

**What the Leader Said Happened**

Connected to the fascist superiority complex is a contempt for feedback,
creating a closed information system that can’t register failure, tolerate
disagreement or revise a plan. Strategy requires accurate reporting, even when
the news is bad, and the willingness to be wrong. Fascist regimes punish the
first and refuse the second.

German high command was still [reporting a controlled
advance](https://research.calvin.edu/german-propaganda-
archive/stalingrad1.htm) in November 1942 when its 6th Army, some [330,000
soldiers](https://www.britannica.com/event/Battle-of-Stalingrad), was being
encircled at Stalingrad. Hitler had declared the city practically taken; the
press never reported the Soviet counteroffensive that surrounded it. When the
remnants finally surrendered on Feb. 2, 1943, it was a [turning point in the
war](https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/timeline-
event/holocaust/1942-1945/german-forces-launch-offensive-against-the-soviet-
union) – Germany’s first catastrophic defeat on the Eastern Front, from which
the Wehrmacht never recovered.

Mussolini bragged about his mighty army of [8 million
soldiers](https://www.lrb.co.uk/the-paper/v20/n01/alexander-stille/eight-
million-bayonets) while [3.5 million](https://www.lrb.co.uk/the-
paper/v42/n10/edward-luttwak/not-uniquely-incompetent) – the real number –
were being routed on three fronts in as many years.

Imperial Japan fused [racial
supremacy](https://www.nationalww2museum.org/war/articles/nazi-germany-
imperial-japan-anti-comintern-pact) with a military code that forbade
surrender and [treated anyone who did as
subhuman](https://www.nationalww2museum.org/war/articles/there-are-no-
civilians-japan). [Loyalty to the emperor was
absolute](https://rikukaigun.org/IJA/IJA%20Field%20Service%20Code%20\(Senjinkun\).html);
questioning his depiction of reality was betrayal.

In that environment, officers had every incentive to lie up the chain of
command when reality on the ground did not match what leaders wanted to hear.
For example, after the Battle of Midway, [a catastrophic
defeat](https://www.nationalww2museum.org/war/topics/battle-of-midway) for
Japan in June 1942, naval [headquarters filed
reports](https://www.usni.org/magazines/naval-history-
magazine/2007/june/ignoring-lessons-defeat) that bore little resemblance to
what happened. Later that year, the Imperial Navy told Tokyo [they had sunk
twelve American
ships](https://www.usni.org/magazines/proceedings/1952/december/strategic-
aspects-battle-formosa) near today’s Taiwan when they had merely damaged two.

Two years of retreat later, [the kamikaze
program](https://www.britannica.com/topic/kamikaze) – which sent some [3,900
pilots](https://www.nationalww2museum.org/war/articles/japans-kamikaze-pilots-
wwii) to their deaths in suicidal crashes against Allied ships – was the
logical conclusion: Let pilots prove their loyalty by dying.![The
Conversation](https://counter.theconversation.com/content/280234/count.gif?distributor=republish-
lightbox-basic)
